subject: Clarify plan options & recommendation for MediaPulse
messages:
From: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@mediapulse.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on tier choices and bundling for MediaPulse

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and caching examples were helpful. We walked the execs through the slides this morning and have a few follow-ups on packaging before procurement opens an RFP: 

- We're unclear on the practical difference between the Compact tier and the Core tier for inference throughput when we have sustained 400 concurrent sessions. Will Compact with burst cover that or do we need Core?
- If we select Core but disable a set of features (multi-region routing, extended logs retention), how much of a price delta do you usually apply vs full Core?
- Procurement asked whether we can get a blended discount for a 12‑month committed spend if we move from Compact to Core mid‑term.

Can you send a short note with recommended paths (upgrade/downgrade) and a sample two‑scenario quote we can include in the RFP? We aim to finalize vendor shortlist by next Wednesday.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Tom Sanders
Head of ML Platforms, MediaPulse
Procurement: procurement@mediapulse.com

P.S. attaching our internal usage snapshot (not attached here — will share after NDA), and happy to jump on a 30 min call if easier.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@mediapulse.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on tier choices and bundling for MediaPulse

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I want to loop in Priyom for the micro‑sizing guidance: 

- Compact vs Core: Compact is tuned for bursty/variable workloads and uses aggressive batching to reduce unit cost; sustained 400 concurrent sessions with low per‑request latency (<=150ms P95) typically needs Core (or Compact + large burst pool). Compact can sometimes meet the need if you accept slightly higher P95 during peaks and configure a burst reserve, but Core gives predictable throughput.

- Feature gating: we generally quantify feature removals two ways — direct cost savings (example: turning off multi‑region routing removes standby capacity (~6–9% of reserved cost)) and ops/service credit adjustments. As a rule of thumb we model a 5–12% list price reduction for removing non‑critical features; final numbers depend on committed spend and the specific features removed.

- Mid‑term blended discount: yes, we support commit step‑ups. Typical approach is a pro‑rated blended rate across months on the committed budget and a true‑up at month boundaries. We can show a worked example in the quote.

Looping in Priyom (SE) — can you add the micro‑sizing notes and two scenario quotes (Conservative: start Core 6 GPU reserved, Optional: start Compact with 12 GPU burst / upgrade to Core at 60 days)? Lauren, I copied you for commercial & approval to share a draft proposal PDF.

Next steps: I'll set up a 30 min workshop for Monday where we can review numbers live.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@mediapulse.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on tier choices and bundling for MediaPulse

Hi Tom — attaching the short sizing rationale inline below and a pair of quick math examples (see attached proposal PDF for full tables).

Sizing rationale (summary):
- 400 concurrent sessions -> typical token mix 60 tokens/turn, 2 turns/session -> ~48k tokens/minute sustained.
- Core with 6 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs at our Core packing gives consistent P95 < 150ms for that footprint.
- Compact option: 4 reserved GPUs + 12 GPU burst pool; effective cost lower initial month but expect higher variance in P95 during large spikes.

Scenario A — Conservative (recommended for predictable SLAs):
- Core, 6 reserved GPUs, 12‑month commit, list price monthly: $120k -> with 18% commit discount -> $98.4k/mo.
- Remove extended logs retention (90d -> 30d) and disable multi‑region standby: estimated additional concession 7% -> $91.5k/mo effective.

Scenario B — Elastic start (lower entry, buffer to upgrade):
- Compact reserved 4 GPUs + burst 12, 6‑month commit, monthly cost (list): $72k -> with 12% commit discount -> $63.4k/mo.
- If upgrade to Core at month 3, blended rate example included in attached.

Attachments referenced: proposal draft with line‑item math (MediaPulse_Proposal_Draft_Q3.pdf).

Happy to review numbers on Monday. If you can share a short usage CSV (token distribution by hour) before then I can refine the model and offer a firm blended quote.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

2) For Scenario B, can you provide the exact blended monthly rate example if we upgrade at the end of month 3 with the 12‑month overall commitment? That will help our CFO model cashflow.

Looking forward to the workshop Monday 10am PT — can you confirm the calendar invite?

— Tom
